description: Regulation that scales obligations with the potential harm of a use: prohibited, high-risk, transparency-only and minimal tiers in the EU model.
The provider builds and places an AI system on the market; the deployer uses it under its authority. Each carries different duties.
The ability of a competent person to understand, monitor, override and stop an AI system, with the authority and time to do so.
An affected person's ability to challenge an AI-assisted decision and reach a human who can change it.
NIST's voluntary AI Risk Management Framework, organized into Govern, Map, Measure and Manage, with a Generative AI Profile (NIST AI 600-1).
Non-binding principles and codes (OECD, UNESCO, G7 Hiroshima) that shape national laws and company policies.
